description.narrative:
Project Development Objective
The objective of the intervention is to "deliver cash transfer support to Sudanese households affected by expected economic reforms and other short-term shocks". The contribution will support the Government-led Sudan Family Support Programme, and intends to help create fiscal and political space for economic reforms.

The World Bank has applied to Sida for funding to carry out the "Sudan Family Support Program" (SFSP) during the period 2020-2022. The objective of the intervention is to "deliver cash transfer support to Sudanese households affected by expected economic reforms and other short-term shocks". Under the SFSP, 80 % of the Sudanese population will receive cash transfers (5 USD a month over 12 months), in order to create political and fiscal space to implement the economic reforms. The economic reforms, primarily lifting of subsidies on fuel, are expected to have an adverse impact on the Sudanese economy, and the cash transfers under the SFSP will mitigate the economic shock of the subsidy removal. Further, the SFSP will also constitute an important step for Sudan towards debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) Initiative, and will also help stabilize the Sudanese economy. Sida's support to the SFSP will also be an important endorsement of Sudan's current transition towards democracy.
The World Bank will implement the Sudan Family Support Program together with the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning and the Digital Transformation Agency.
The total budget of the intervention is 2.07 billion USD, out of which the World Bank contributes with approximately 410 million USD. Donors have currently pledged around 415 million USD to the SFSP, and further funding rounds are to be expected. Other donors include Germany, the UK, the EU, Norway, Ireland, Italy, France, Spain, Canada, the Netherlands, Malta, the UAE and Saudi Arabia. 1.9 billion of the total budget will be forwarded from the World Bank to the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning. Sida plans to support the Sudan Family Support Program with a contribution of 200 MSEK. In addition, approximately 25.5 MSEK from Sida's, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry for Environment's respective Donor Balance Accounts have been reallocated to SFSP. The Swedish contribution to the SFSP thus totals approximately 225.5 MSEK.

Världsbanken har ansökt till Sida om finansiering för att genomföra 'Sudan Family Support Program' (SFSP) under perioden 2020-2022. Insatsens mål är att "distribuera kontantstöd till sudanesiska hushåll negativt påverkade av kommande ekonomiska reformer och andra chocker". Inom ramen för SFSP kommer 80 % av den sudanesiska befolkningen att mottaga kontantstöd (5 US-dollar per månad över tolv månader), med målet att skapa politiska och ekonomiska förusättningar för att implementera de ekonomiska reformerna. De ekonomiska reformerna, framförallt eliminering av bränslesubventioner, förväntas ha negativa konsekvenser på den sudanesiska ekonomin. Kontantstödet under SFSP kommer därmed att mildra de ekonomiska konsekvenserna av nämnda eliminering av subventioner. Stödet till SFSP kommer även utgöra en viktig milstolpe för Sudans strävan att nå skuldavskrivningar inom ramen för HIPC-initiativet ("Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative"), och kommer även att vara ett viktigt led för att stabilisera Sudans ekonomi. Slutligen bedöms Sidas stöd till SFSP vara ett starkt och viktigt ställningstagande för Sudans demokratiska transition.
SFSP kommer att implementeras av Världsbanken i samarbete med Sudans Finansministerium och Sudans Myndighet för Digital Utveckling.
Den totala budgeten för SFSP uppgår till 2,07 miljarder US-dollar. Världsbanken ämnar bidra med uppskattningsvis 410 miljoner US-dollar och bilaterala givare har gett utfästelser om 415 miljoner US-dollar. Ytterligare finansieringsrundor är att vänta framöver. Andra givare inkluderar Tyskland, Storbritannien, EU, Norge, Irland, Italien, Frankrike, Spanien, Kanada, Nederländerna, Malta, Förenade Arabemiraten och Saudiarabien. 1,9 miljarder US-dollar av den totala budgeten kommer att vidareförmedlas från Världsbanken till Finansministeriet. Sidas planerade stöd till SFSP omfattar 200 miljoner kronor. I tillägg har Sida, Miljödepartementet och Utrikesdepartementet överfört totalt cirka 25,5 miljoner kronor från givarbalanskonton hos Världsbanken till SFSP. Det totala svenska bidraget till SFSP uppgår därmed till cirka 225,5 miljoner kronor.

This update is based on the last narrative trust fund report, i.e. the Annual Report 2023, which covered the period of January 2022 - June 2023. STARS was designed to support Sudans economic and peace building transition and build country delivery systems, including for crisis response. The following four thematic areas are: - Social protection - Economic revival and better governance - Resilience and basic services - Crisis response
The transition has been accompanied by economic difficulties and deteriorating living conditions, COVID19 pandemic, flood, the military takeover of October 25, 2021, and the military confrontation between the two rivals, SAF and RSF, that started on April 15, 2023. STARS was previously administered by the World Bank and operated in close partnership with government and development partners through the Partnership Council (PC). Due to the pause, the configuration of the PC changed. Government is no longer participating nor co[1]chairing PC meetings with the Bank until normalisation. Furthermore, the military takeover also led to a pause in operations, including STARS-supported projects, and the triggering of the World Bank Operational Policy (OP) 7.30: Dealing with De Facto Governments, which is still in force. With these challenges in mind, STAR performed as follows according to thematic areas:
Social protection Social Protection (SP) was the largest thematic area of focus before the operations paused in October 2021 and remained the largest area with four activities: Project Preparation Grant (PPG) for SFSP, the SFSP, Technical Assistance (TA) and Diagnostics for SFSP, and SESNP. Only The Sudan Emergency Safety Net Project (SESNP) is under implementation but the armed conflict since April 2023, has slowed down project implementation. Nevertheless, SESNP provided social assistance through in kind food and cash transfer to 2,143,366 most food insecure people across 12 states, exceeding the target of 2 million. The project reached 1,984,759 beneficiaries through the cash based transfers (exceeding the target by 5 percent) and 158,607 beneficiaries through in kind food transfers (exceeding the target by nearly 60 percent).
About 60 percent of the in kind food and cash beneficiaries were female, respectively, exceeding the target by nearly 10 percentage points. In West and Central Darfur State, reports show that more than 80 percent of the cash recipients were women. About 3 percent of the beneficiaries were persons with disabilities. Over 70 percent beneficiaries under the cash based transfers sub-component were residents while 30 percent were internally displaced populations while through in kind transfers, 55 residents and 45 percent internally displaced populations were reached.
Lastly, on enhancing safety nets delivery systems, about 1.38 million beneficiaries have biometric registration, close to the target of 1.5 million. Access constraints due to the rainy season and roads conditions have been experienced, impacting staff travelling to the biometric registration sites as well as the people reaching the sites to be registered. The utilization of digital payments systems increased the number of beneficiaries enrolled in mobile money, reaching 101,860 beneficiaries (5 percent which is below the intermediate results indicator target of 10 percent)
Economic revival and better governance The focus area supported three activities: (i) TA to the Sudan Social Security Investment Authority that was fully disbursed and closed on June 30, 2022 and (ii) Sudan Household Survey which closed on June 30, 2023 without progress given the pause and (iii) the Analytical Program on Productivity, Resilience and Growth to be undertaken in FY24.
Crisis response The focus area has two activities: COVID19 Emergency Response Project (RETF) and Sudan Emergency Response Project (BETF). Due to the pause on disbursements to Government, project activities were not implemented, and consequently limited progress was made focused on training and support for frontline health workers to deliver essential health services. 94 (34 male and 60 female) staff were trained of the target of 1 000. It is worth mention that the fund supported COVID-19 Emergency Response Project (CERP) which contributed to the deployment of 9 million COVID19 vaccines to cover nearly 19.31 percent of the targeted population (12.20 percent fully vaccinated, 6.59 percent partially vaccinated, and 0.69 percent received a booster dose).
Concluding remarks Sida notes that the abovementioned challenges clearly affected the ability to complete programme activities. Only two out of nine activities performed as planned. The biggest success was the Sudan Emergency Safety Net Project (SESNP) and as described in lessons learned, much due to WFPs capacity as an appropriate third party implementer. In implementing the SESNP, the WFP has contributed to building the national capacity by involving Sudanese nationals in project delivery to create a critical mass and built on existing systems and instruments (e.g., MIS, targeting and biometric registration, GRM, payment systems) to facilitate transferability to government once the pause is lifted. Lessons from this report was integral in repurposing the activities of STARS to the new Sudan Somoud Community Resilience Project, which was developed in response the new context of widespread armed conflict.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
